threads.body: The stated reason is inaccurate. Aggregating child-call breakdowns into one agent value loses the model and call context needed to interpret them, but it does not inherently count tokens more than once. Double counting occurs only if a consumer sums parent and child spans, and that applies equally to the total token attributes retained here. Describe the loss of context instead.

threads.body: Splitting out these groups removes their attributes from the internal `invoke_agent` table, but the retained `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` reference still inherits the registry note whose example lists cache and modality attributes. As a result, the generated internal-span documentation at lines 628-634 advertises attributes that this change has just excluded. Override that note for the internal span, or split the total-usage reference so this span gets guidance that only discusses total tokens.

threads.body: Calling these breakdowns "only meaningful per inference call" conflicts with the client `invoke_agent` span, which still defines both cache and modality breakdowns at lines 530-531 for provider-reported remote-agent totals. Scope the restriction to internal call-tree aggregation so the generated guidance does not rule out another supported span.

threads.body:
The client `invoke_agent` span keeps both attributes, so "on agent spans" overstates the removal.

```suggestion
Remove `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens` from the internal `invoke_agent` span. Cache breakdowns on that span aggregate across models and inference calls, which makes them misleading; consumers should aggregate them from `gen_ai.inference.client` spans instead.
```
